title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
The page continues a list, begun on p.41, of the realization data attached to a 'family of motives' over a base S (a Q-variety). The motivic Galois group G is a reductive Q-group. The list on p.43 gives the plan:

A) The group G.
B) A principal G-bundle P over S with integrable connection. This is the de Rham realization with its Gauss–Manin connection.
C) The Betti structure: reduction of the structure group of P^an_C from G(C) to G(Q). Fix a base point xi_0 and a point x_0 of P(xi_0). Then this becomes a monodromy representation w: Gamma = pi_1(S(C),xi_0) -> G(Q), together with the horizontal developing map q: S̄_C -> P^an_C, which satisfies q(s̄gamma) = q(s̄)w(gamma). The reduced torsor is P̃_C = S̄_C x^Gamma G(Q).
D) A period map. p.41 gives it as a holomorphic f: P̃_C -> Y_G with f(xg) = g^{-1}f(x). Here Y_G is the space of Hodge structures on G_R (morphisms Deligne torus S -> G_R) compatible with a fixed weight cocharacter. f must also be compatible with the Hodge-filtration torsor P_S (a reduction of P to the 'Hodge' group, i.e. a parabolic/filtration subgroup) and the trivialization p(x).

This page first rewrites D) on the universal cover. Via w and q, f becomes a holomorphic map f: S̄_C -> Y_G with f(s̄gamma) = w(gamma)^{-1}f(s̄). For every s̄, f(s̄): S -> G_R must be compatible with P_S and the induced point of P_S(C). This is exactly the equivariant period map of a variation of Hodge structure with Mumford–Tate group inside G, valued in a G(R)-homogeneous Mumford–Tate domain.

Grothendieck then adds the arithmetic datum E). This is a 'restriction' (descent) of the covering P̃_C x^{G(Q)} G(A_f) over S^an_C to a covering with group G(A_f) over S itself. The margin says A = finite adèles over Q. In group terms: factor Gamma -> G(Q) -> G(A_f) through Gamma -> pi_1(S,xi_0) -> G(A_f). That is, the profinite completion of topological monodromy extends to the arithmetic étale fundamental group: a compatible system of l-adic realizations assembled adelically, comparable with Betti via Artin's comparison.

Finally there is a compatibility on component groups. The finite covering P̃_C x^{G(Q)} (G/G^0)(A_f) is associated to P̃_C/G^0(Q) = (P/G^0)^an_C. This is the analytification of the finite étale S-scheme P/G^0. So its descent to S is already determined by the algebraic datum B); the adelic datum must agree with it.

The next page summarizes A)–E). It asserts that A), B), C) plus f at a point over the generic point should determine D) and E) when everything comes from a category of motives. It then asks for an analytic continuation formula for f, and for the relation between D) and E), with 'automorphic functions?'.

The problem served is to axiomatize the full set of realizations (de Rham + connection, Betti, Hodge, adelic étale) of a family of motives over S with given motivic Galois group G. This is the 'motivic' structure later visible in Shimura data (G, X, G(A_f)) and in Deligne's absolute Hodge cycles framework.
errors: Condition b) is written f(xg) = w(g)^{-1} f(x) 'pour s ∈ S'. On the universal cover it should read f(s̄gamma) = w(gamma)^{-1} f(s̄) for s̄ ∈ S̄_C and gamma ∈ Gamma; the variables are copied from the P̃ version.

Griffiths transversality (horizontality of the Hodge filtration relative to the connection) is not imposed. Holomorphy plus G(Q)-equivariance plus pointwise compatibility with P_S does not by itself make f the period map of a variation of Hodge structure. Note this transversality condition was not yet in the literature in 1965 (Griffiths 1968).

The compatibility of the adelic datum E) with the Betti datum is stated only via the factorization Gamma -> pi_1(S,xi_0). No compatibility between the Hodge datum D) and E) is given; the next page lists it as an open question.
The text trails off ('celle donnée plus haut....'). The argument that the G/G^0 part of E) is already determined by B) is not completed.

ideas.what: Period map of a family of motives as a G(Q)-equivariant holomorphic map from the universal cover to the space Y_G of Hodge structures on G_R (Deligne torus -> G_R) compatible with a weight
ideas.modern_name: Period map to a Mumford–Tate domain; variation of Hodge structure with Mumford–Tate group in G
ideas.usually_credited_to: Griffiths (1968–70) for period domains/maps; Mumford (1966) and Deligne (1971–72) for the Deligne-torus/group-theoretic formulation; Green–Griffiths–Kerr for Mumford–Tate domains

ideas.what: Data of a family of motives as a G-torsor with integrable connection, a Betti reduction to G(Q) given by monodromy, and a Hodge-filtration reduction P_S
ideas.modern_name: Tannakian description of variations of (motivic) realizations; Gauss–Manin G-torsor with monodromy
ideas.usually_credited_to: Saavedra Rivano (1972), Deligne (1972 'La conjecture de Weil pour les surfaces K3', 1982 'Hodge cycles on abelian varieties'), Deligne–Milne
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's motivic Galois group ideas were transmitted via Saavedra's thesis; this specific relative formulation is not known to be published by him.

ideas.what: Adelic arithmetic datum: factorization Gamma -> G(Q) -> G(A_f) through the étale fundamental group pi_1(S,xi_0) of S over Q, i.e. descent of the G(A_f)-covering to S
ideas.modern_name: Compatible system of l-adic realizations as a representation pi_1^et(S) -> G(A_f); canonical models of Shimura varieties
ideas.usually_credited_to: Shimura (canonical models, 1960s), Deligne ('Travaux de Shimura' 1971, 'Variétés de Shimura' 1979)

ideas.what: Compatibility on the component group: the covering associated with (G/G^0)(A_f) equals the analytification of the finite étale cover P/G^0 of S
ideas.modern_name: Component group of the motivic/Mumford–Tate group and its Galois action (motivic pi_0)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne, Serre (connected components of l-adic monodromy / Mumford–Tate groups)

missed.claim: In 1965 Grothendieck packages a family of motives with motivic Galois group G as (G, an equivariant period map to Hodge structures on G_R, an adelic G(A_f) descent over S). This is structurally the Shimura-datum-plus-canonical-model package that Deligne formalized in 1971–79. On the next page he explicitly asks for the relation between the Hodge datum and the adelic datum, suggesting 'automorphic functions'. A motivic Galois–Shimura–automorphic link in Grothendieck's own hand this early is not part of the standard historical account.
missed.quote: on se donne une factorisation de Γ → G(Q) → G(A) par Γ → π1(S,ξ0) → G(A)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical credit for the origin of the motivic interpretation of Shimura varieties (G-motives with level structure). The question 'relation between D) and E)' is essentially the problem of how Hodge data determine Galois data: absolute Hodge cycles, Mumford–Tate vs. l-adic monodromy.

missed.claim: The adjacent NB claims that A), B), C) and the value of f at one point over the generic point should determine the full period map and the adelic datum for objects coming from motives. This is a rigidity/determination statement (Hodge data at one point determine Galois data). It is related to the Mumford–Tate conjecture and Deligne's absolute Hodge results, and was left open by Grothendieck.
missed.quote: Quand au revêtement P̃_C ×^{G(Q)} (G/G^0)(A), il est associé à P̃_C/G^0(Q) = (P/G^0)^an_C
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A precise relative form ('generic-point Hodge data + connection determine the adelic G(A_f)-system') sits close to open problems: Mumford–Tate conjecture in families, and motivic versions of André's theorems on monodromy.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an early, explicit axiomatization of a family of motives via its G-torsor, Betti reduction, equivariant period map to Hodge structures on G_R, and adelic Galois descent. It anticipates Shimura data and canonical models (Deligne 1971/79) and Mumford–Tate domains. The link to automorphic functions on the following page sharpens this. The details are sketchy, transversality is missing, and the content partly overlaps with ideas known to have reached Deligne, so the surprise is moderate.
transcription_corrections: 'on se donne une "rationalité"' is more plausibly 'une "restriction"' (descent of the covering to S), consistent with 'Restriction de P̃ ×^{G(Q)} G(A) à S' on p.43.
'revêtement de rev. ... de groupe G(Q_ℓ) sur S' should probably read 'revêtement ... de groupe G(A) sur S'; the margin defines A as finite adèles and the next page uses G(A).
'Quand au revêtement' should be 'Quant au revêtement'.
In b) the variables are x, g but the intended meaning is s̄ ∈ S̄_C and gamma ∈ Gamma. The inserted '{+pour s ∈ S+}' looks like 'pour s̄ ∈ S̄' (or 'g ∈ Γ').
'G_Hodge[?]' is uncertain; it likely denotes the subgroup (parabolic/filtration group) to which P_S reduces the structure group, as on p.41.
